name: The Great Collection
years: ~200–310 Si (with roots at the Edict, ~80 Si)
summary: The Censer's century-long campaign to seize every Glimmerborn and every written word of the old song on Aurelith. It began as scattered purges and became a machine: watchlists, seizure convoys, archive-vaults, and the quiet invention of an enemy market. The Collection nearly succeeded — and its overflow created everything it was meant to prevent: the Hollow Mile's black market, the Rememberers' Chain of Memory, and the continent's permanent habit of fear.

participants.name: the-censer
participants.note: wardens, incense-bearers, and the first watchlists

participants.name: the-rememberers
participants.note: Ithyn's heirs, organized into the Chain of Memory by the purge itself

participants.name: the-hollow-mile
participants.note: every seizure made a buyer; every buyer made a fence

participants.name: realms of the Silence
participants.note: signatory courts supplied wagons, jails, and silence

course_of_events.what: The first Reeve bans written Old Weaver. Penalty: a year of silence, sewn mouth or exile, by whim. The Collection has its legal ground.

Coordinated seizures across every realm at once — Glimmerborn taken at birth from Moonwarden birth-ledgers, books burned by the wagonload. The overflow of forgeries and duplicates finds buyers under Velkash's bridges: the Hollow Mile is born.

Watchlists standardize; seizure convoys run scheduled routes; the archive-quarter rises in Velkash on a burned college's foundation. Its deepest wing receives 'the silent ones' — no record says in what condition.

The final sweep: every Old Weaver text the Censer can find, seized in a single season. Nearly complete. The survivors of the purge formalize the Chain of Memory — texts copied thrice, cells of three, no cell knowing two others — and go underground for four hundred years.
Few Glimmerborn remain; fewer are found. The song is a rumor. The Collection ends not with victory but with nothing left to collect — the Grey Peace.

key_places.name: The Archive Quarter
key_places.description: The Censer's walled vaults in Velkash, built on a destroyed college's foundation. Its deepest wing holds the silent ones — and, some say, still receives deliveries.

key_places.name: The Hollow Mile
key_places.description: Born from the purge's overflow: the mile of tunnels beneath Velkash's bridges where everything seized developed a second, purchasable life.

key_places.name: The White Roads' Stumps
key_places.description: The Concord's white paved roads were pulled up for firewood during the Falling Kingdoms; purge convoys later used the stumps as route-markers. Sections survive in the Wealdmark.

key_places.name: The Chain Wells
key_places.description: Rememberer meeting-places disguised as wells, ruins, and root-cellars across three realms. No complete list has ever existed — by design.

consequences: Open Glimmerborn nearly extinct by the Grey Peace — the Waking's later shock.
Old Weaver survives only in the Chain of Memory and the Censer's own forbidden archives.
The Hollow Mile becomes permanent: prohibition's economy outlives the prohibition's zeal.
Birth-ledgers become surveillance — and the Moonwardens become reluctant collaborators.
remembrance: Uncommemorated by design; the Silence erases its own history. Survives inverted: 'a year of silence' as curse, the Road-Singers' forbidden verse about the wagons, and the Rememberers' motto — 'the song is not lost; it is hidden.'
adventure_hooks: A purge-era seizure convoy's manifest surfaces: one item listed was never archived. All three claimants want players to fetch it.
An aged Moonwarden holds the original falsified birth-ledgers — proof that hundreds listed as born elsewhere were Glimmerborn saved by her order.
The Chain's oldest cell keeps a vacancy: a memorizer died with a song unpassed. Players must find someone willing to learn it — and bear it.
